channel.title: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)" - A millipede that is a germaphobe

item.title: Re: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded: I see. I've updated it based on some of the other feedback I've gotten and I think it might be better now.

item.title: Re: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Why is it a millipede?

Hmmm… I haven't given that one much consideration. (As I think you can tell.) I think that the thing that inspired me to make it a millipede was a picture I saw of a giant extinct millipede species. Maybe it could be one of those that managed to survive somehow.

Why does it attack things?

Again, not sure. In fact I think I'm going to scrap that part entirely. Maybe it's just a weird millipede germaphobe. I think that I actually like that better. Thanks!

Why is it a germaphobe?

Ok, this is my favorite part. It's a germaphobe because in this universe a plague was what wiped out the rest of it's species. (Man they could have really used 049.) It was the only one who could fend off the plague using it's anomalous properties.

This is actually the most interesting aspect at the moment

I know.

maybe give it cleaning supplies and have it join the site cleaning crew.

Haha! Actually that might be a good idea… especially if that's it's only anomalous property. Come to think of it I actually really like that idea.

I'm going to change the SCP Idea to be a millipede that is able to kill all germs that are near it. (Exact distance yet to be determined.) Scrap everything else this is what the idea is now. Thank you for the ideas! I have edited the original post to represent this.

item.title: Re: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Some questions and info that might help you see the issues here, and point you down a more productive path:

Why is it a millipede? Not just in the mechanical sense, but why, for the purposes of the story, is it a millipede rather than a centipede, or a robot, or a bowl of nachos with legs? There should be a why, at least in your mental notes. If there isn't: Why is it a millipede?

Why does it attack things? Again, if there isn't a reason: Why does it attack things?

Why is it a germaphobe? (This is actually the most interesting aspect at the moment, btw. Zero sarcasm: maybe give it cleaning supplies and have it join the site cleaning crew.)

What makes this an SCP? The Foundation has loads of giant bugs in containment. What makes this one require Special containment procedures instead of "lock it up and feed it periodically"

Potentially relevant info regarding millipedes: In the early days of land-dwelling life, millipedes were some of the largest creatures on Earth, some species measuring around 2 meters. They had no known predators. Almost all species of millipede (past and present) are herbivores. Their survival mechanisms are almost entirely defensive measures- they curl up, some taste bad or excrete mildly irritating chemicals, some have bristles…it's all protection, no offense. Some of the most harmless creatures on earth, really.

item.title: Re: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Sadly this is not gonna work as a main site article in its current state. It feels very much like a series one article, which follows a format the site has long moved from. I highly recommend reading more into the 5000 series of articles, which really highlight the focus on storytelling as opposed to just a strange object.

What you have presented is unfortunately not only basic and not very interesting but something that has already been done before (but with a millipede coating). The hatred for organic life? Yea we got SCP-682 and many others that hate organic life, it kills, kills and kills? That's not very entertaining on its own. You need to rethink this idea, a LOT. Think of a story, maybe the millipede was once a person or something? (very basic idea). Explore different stories you wanna tell and use your SCP as the vessel of that story.

item.title: Re: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
What actually are the anomalous properties?

It's anomalous properties are the fact that it kills all harmful germs within a certain distance and it is larger than a normal millipede

a SCP article is a story disguised as a technical report

I have edited my first post so it's better.

item.title: Re: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
A large millipede esque creature with anomalous properties

you describe it as 'esque' here but as a 'millipede' alone in the next sentence so like…is it just not quite a millipede cos of the anomalous properties? What actually are the anomalous properties? Is it just the things you've laid out in the Central Narrative?

Central Narrative:

Okay so really what I want to see out of this is like…a rough idea of what the actual article is gonna contain. My concern here is that your intent is just to like…describe a weird thing which really will not fly nowadays: remember a SCP article is a story disguised as a technical report, not an encyclopedia entry on a weird thing; and stuff like this is always better when shown.

At the end of the day: that's my biggest concern with this concept. Without showing us why this weird thing is interesting in some manner, it's not going to be interesting.

item.title: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Elevator Pitch: A large millipede that is friendly to humans and kills all harmful germs near it.

Central Narrative: A millipede that is about 3 feet long that kills all microscopic life near it. When germs are talked about near it it expresses displeasure and will move to the door to try to get out and clean the germs off of the walls. It also seems to only target germs that are harmful to humans and leaves beneficial germs alone.

Hook: It will be a kind light hearted SCP that is just a germaphobe. It is also of use to The Foundation as a cleaner.
